content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a standard load cell providing a 0-10V signal via an amplifier into AI3. With the correct span and offset, I see values from 0-1000 for a 100kg load cell, giving a resolution of 100g. The cell is overrated for safety, despite its overload tolerance. My question is: can I configure [product_name] so the ADC's 1000 values cover just the 0-5V portion of the analog input, effectively doubling the resolution for my working range to 50g? What's the best approach to achieve this? Kind regards, [user_name]
No, that's not possible. The resolution cannot be changed. An input change of 0.01 V always remains one unit after the A/D conversion.

Thank you for responding. I'm not clear on what you mean by 0.01V. My goal isn't to change the resolution of [product_name] but to clamp the input range to 0-5V and apply the 10-bit measurement to this truncated voltage. Are you saying that 0-1000 always maps to the full input range? How does offset and multiplier affect this? A flowchart would help.

For [product_name]'s analog input, the A/D converter maps any input (current, voltage, or PT100/1000 sensor) to 0-1000 units. For a 0-10V signal, each 0.01V equals one unit (10V divided by 1000). If you only process 0-5V, you get 0-500 units, so the resolution stays the same—0.01V per unit. It's not possible to change this via software.

Check the online help in [product_name] engineering software for guidance; there's information about handling analog signals. To improve overall resolution, you'd need to choose a more suitable sensor or install a signal converter between the sensor and input. For example, selecting a sensor with a narrower range increases your measurement resolution. Alternatively, a signal amplifier with adjustable gain and offset could help. Regards, [user_name]

Hi, [user_name]'s advice is correct: you cannot change the input resolution in [product_name] itself. The only real solution is to use a load cell scaled for your range (for instance, 0-10V for 0-50kg). Make sure to check accuracy as well. According to the [product_name] manual, expect a typical error limit of around ±1.5%. Hope this helps.

Thanks all. I have a load cell amplifier, and I've set analog zero to the lowest point, with payload at 62/1000. I'm used to programming software where you can truncate the scale and multiply analog input before feeding the ADC, which is why I thought about configuring [product_name]'s input to 0-5V to pump up resolution. Setting for 0-50kg could be risky in an industrial setting. I reviewed the documentation and vaguely recall a 0-5V input option—it might have been a different brand manual though. In any case, seems it's not feasible, so thanks again.

Configurable analog inputs would be great. Some PLC systems like [version_no] controllers offer this, but at a much higher cost. There are requests for [product_name] analog modules with better accuracy, but no one knows when—or if—they'll become available. If you're using [product_name] with network features, you can investigate remote analog modules that work with Modbus TCP/IP. Regards, [user_name]

We used an analog sensor with a 0-10V output over a range of -20°C to 100°C (accuracy 0.12°C when sampled by [product_name] as 0-1000 units). We fed this signal through a 2x gain amplifier (DIN rail, includes ESD protection, runs on +12V from [product_name]). This adjusted the range to -20°C to 40°C, improving accuracy to 0.06°C. Since our sensor mainly operated between 16°C and 30°C, the extra resolution was helpful. Remember that in [product_name], scaling involves offset and multiplier adjustments.
Great approach. It would be simple if [product_name] offered a software setting for a 0-5V input to accomplish this!

I've used [product_name] for many years. Sometimes you want finer analog resolution, and I believe it’s technically feasible in firmware. But consider: higher resolution usually means higher cost. Also, many users lack experience dealing with the challenges of accurate analog measurements (EMC/EMV interference). The default 1000-step resolution in [product_name] meets my needs; if I need higher, I switch to larger systems. But everyone’s requirements differ.

Agreed. My point is that 10-bit resolution is sufficient, but having user control over input range (clamping/truncation) would improve flexibility. This function doesn't require hardware changes—just code updates managing input parameters. For current/voltage conversion, you can use a resistor, but my suggestion is even simpler. All the best, [user_name]

Your request makes sense, but [product_name] does not have this feature. Physical analog signals are digitized using a 10-bit ADC, which is limited to 1000 steps, and this determines your resolution. Software can't remap the range so that 0.01V equals only part of the load cell's full range.

It's not possible to increase A/D converter resolution through software. You can truncate results to get a 0-500 range, but the step size remains the same. If higher analog resolution is needed, you must use hardware like a different sensor or a signal amplifier, or choose a controller with a more suitable input range. For current signals (0/4-20mA), proper resistor selection is crucial, as many sensors have maximum load limits. Sometimes, it's most efficient to buy a new sensor with the required range. Regards, [user_name]

The translation may be off: The bit resolution isn't changed, but narrowing the measured range increases precision within that window. In audio terms, it's like oversampling—reducing the bandwidth increases quantization detail. For [product_name], a 0-5V input measured with 10-bit ADC would use the full set of digital values over a smaller voltage window. This would require a software switch mapping the ADC to a narrower range. Am I misunderstanding something?

These are not equivalent—audio sampling and analog input measurement in PLCs work differently. If you're unsure despite the feedback here, consider submitting a support request to [company_name] directly. Marking this topic as 'Support Relevant'.

I fully admit I may be missing something, given my background is audio engineering. I appreciate everyone's explanations—even if the analog-to-digital conversion processes for audio and weight sensors differ, I'd love clarification for everyone's benefit. Thank you all for your patience and insights.

All relevant points have been covered. The analog input range (0-10V) in [product_name] is always mapped to 0-1000 units, and there is no option to set the measuring range to 0-5V. Measuring 5V simply equates to 500 units on the input scale.

Audio signals are handled differently; they have fixed peak-to-peak values and resolution is managed by filtering and sampling frequency. In automation, analog signals are measured for their magnitude, not for time-domain analysis. Regards, [user_name]

You are correct—it's confusing to compare time and amplitude domains. Expressed as amplitude: halving the input voltage increases quantization accuracy. However, anything above the threshold is effectively clipped. My suggestion was to allow [product_name] to ignore voltages above a set limit, so the ADC only focuses on the desired range. I understand this isn't available at present, and thanks everyone for the explanations and patience.

Ideally, an ADC with configurable maximum measurement value would help in these cases, but in practice it’s handled by additional hardware, like a pre-amplifier. This adds cost—alternatively, select a sensor with the needed range to save expense. For more advanced needs, use a PLC with higher resolution analog inputs, such as [version_no] modules. Regards, [user_name]

Thank you; for most of my tasks, [product_name] works well—it's easy to program and cost-effective for small tasks and web interfaces. Moving up to a more capable PLC is expensive for just a bit more analog resolution. For example, some AC drives have 12-bit analog inputs, but lack simplicity and built-in web servers. One last question: If a voltage over the input range (e.g. 0-12V) is supplied, and there's no input filter, what happens? Is this handled by hardware? Maybe a sensor with Modbus output could do external processing, but then using a more advanced PLC may be easier overall.
Note: The base module's analog input can also function as a digital input for 24VDC (maximum 26.8VDC). Just a thought—any other questions?

analysis.insight_summary: A user hopes to boost analog input resolution for a controller by mapping its ADC's entire scale to just half of the input voltage range, effectively doubling measurement precision. Multiple participants explain that this isn't possible within [product_name] due to hardware limits: resolution is fixed and cannot be adjusted via software. Suggestions focus on hardware modifications—like choosing sensors with narrower ranges or adding amplifiers—to improve practical measurement resolution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants an option in the controller or its software to remap the ADC's full range to just a portion of the analog input (e.g., 0-5V), thereby increasing resolution for more precise measurements within that band.
